bit.title: Prove the sharp finite-stage BIT bootstrap and the supplier thresholds required for kappa = 0.005
bit.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove the sharp finite-stage frontier of the completed ordinary BIT wrapper,
then work backward from kappa=1/200 to the stronger covered supplier it needs.
**No new kappa.** The selected result remains .00363005817 (#7000/#7001).

For rational 0<=b<C<1/2 and fixed stage depth h, the full three-term source
cost has one-stage supremum F_C(b)=C/(1+C-b). It is not attained under strict
slack. With y=C^h(C-b)/(1-b), the h-stage supremum is (C-y)/(1-y); the proof
gives the exact inverse target test and rational witnesses below that bound.
An acyclic portfolio using covered prices at most C cannot cross C.

From selected b=.00385248, one stage reaching .005 needs covered
C>3112961/621875000. A hypothetical C=.0050001 needs exactly two stages;
explicit rho=.0051 choices reach ordinary .00500007. The current covered
.0038525298 and atom rho=.004 cannot fund the target. This is a limitation
of the frozen cost interface, not a universal BIT lower bound.

## Full costs and target join

The bill retains e^(1-rho), e^((1-rho)(1-C)+rho(1-b)), and e^rho log(e),
all multiplied by complete volume and a fresh finite constant. Completed
predecessors, input-dependent stock depth, whole-job routing, restoration,
fixed thresholds and all spectator contracts remain required.

The hypothetical BIT output joins uniform complex .00500006 in the actual
54 strict and four functional outer checks. A separate input-lift proof
repairs the old sufficient guard through .0051. No stronger covered BIT or
complex native is constructed. This is not complete conditional .005.

## Sources and verification

Canonical base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Nine exact input
Git/SHA256 pins bind the selected review, delayed-cover proof, finite ordinary
bootstrap, current checker and Nick Petalas's prior outer-region theorem.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-target-bootstrap/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/bit-target-bootstrap/independent.py
```

Both also passed with -O on authenticated source exports. Author checks cover
1,520 exact identities,18,810 full-cost comparisons and570 witnesses; the
independent matrix derivation checks450 cases and5,000 comparisons. Controls
reject zero slack, omitted adapter/stock, one-stage overclaim and unfunded BIT.
Expected markers: PASS_TARGET_BIT_BOOTSTRAP and PASS_INDEPENDENT_BOOTSTRAP_REVIEW.
The generic registry runner was not executed in this source-export environment.

## Limits and credit

All five foundational assumptions remain. No whole supplier replay, new native,
selected-frontier update, human peer review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.
Credit Rohan Arun's #185 lineage, BagMan9's #768 tied-depth precedent, T37,
zxv, Cinna Davis, Jacob Alan Sussman, DreamingOfClouds and the current source
authors. The decoupled atom/covered optimum differs from the prior tied affine
recurrence. Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance; separate
model-assisted adversarial review. Apache-2.0.

owned.title: Prove the paid-rank versus scalar-work floor for all 23 selected owned rises (no new kappa)
owned.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove a paid-rank versus scalar-work obstruction for isolated replacements of
all 23 owned rises in selected #7000. **No new kappa.** This excludes a specific
tempting route to .005, not that target or joint rewrites generally.

Every actual rise has a nonzero coefficient of an independent public array.
Complex-array surjectivity, or spanning scaled inputs on exact grids, forces
a single-input replacement to implement the complete prescribed map.

## Exact result and target relevance

At column count f, a linear replacement with g whole-field ADDs and Gaussian
children of total rank s has row support at most 2^(g+s*f). The rank-r return
has 2^(r*f) equal-modulus entries. Squared operator error is at least
max(0,1-2^(g-(r-s)*f)); exactness or error below 1/sqrt(2) requires
g>=(r-s)*f. Arbitrary monomial maps/scalars and independent scratch are allowed;
external data-dependent side information is excluded.

At t=199/200, paid moment below r^t implies s<r, hence at least f ADDs.
Fixed native templates cannot do this for all f; literal full-field scans cost
Omega(V*f), exceeding O(V*f^t*polylog(f)). Fused/partial-field algorithms and
changed boundaries remain outside scope. The r*f-ADD butterfly is checked
as the admitted scalar escape.

The 23-rise histogram has rank mass56 per native. Removing all 18 occurrences
for free would move the actual moment from about -567.716011 to +434.821363.
The theorem blocks funding that relaxation through these isolated lower-rank
replacements. Joint correlations, changed trajectories, productive targets and
new interfaces remain possible. The selected Gaussian factorization is inherited,
not inferred from binary frame dimension alone.

## Sources and verification

Canonical base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. The complete source
word and invoice have exact Git/SHA256 pins in SOURCES.json. Forward rows and
an independent reverse-prefix adjoint match all 23 pivots and support sizes 79-314.
Independent checks cover 1,095 frame bases, 71,261 events and 54 lifetimes.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/independent_budget.py
```

Normal/-O author and independent checks passed on exact source exports.
Controls include wrong phase, omitted axis, dependent frame, altered pivot,
undercharged rise and the full-price scalar escape. Independent exact roots
confirm the target budget. Expected markers: PASS_SELECTED_OWNED_RANK_TRADEOFF,
PASS_INDEPENDENT_REVERSE_OWNED_AUDIT and PASS_INDEPENDENT_OWNED_BUDGET.
No full native catalogue cold replay or generic registry run is claimed.

## Limits and credit

All five foundational assumptions remain; no complete conditional .005 or
unconditional theorem. Credit #6914's paid owned-ascent realization,
Matarener's #5445 historical nested floor, Nick Petalas's #5111 sparse-row
approximation and #679's volume warnings, plus #7000/#7001 and their full
native/helper/compiler lineage. Classical support counting is credited.
Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance and separate
model-assisted adversarial review. Apache-2.0; no human/kernel acceptance.
